claims.text: The starting catalyst contains multiple principal elements in nearly equiatomic ratios and has minimal platinum-group-metal loading.
An ultra-thin, conformal ceria overcoat can be deposited on the catalyst by atomic layer deposition.
The deposited ceria layer forms oxygen-vacancy interfaces.
The deposited ceria layer acts as a physical barrier that stabilizes the catalyst structure.
The ceria overcoat promotes oxygen-storage capacity.
The ceria overcoat inhibits nanoparticle sintering.
The ceria overcoat inhibits thermal degradation.
Oxygen vacancies in the ceria overcoat facilitate catalytic redox reactions.
Suppression of sintering and enhanced redox behavior preserve the catalyst's active sites.
Preserving active sites with the ceria overcoat lowers the need for additional platinum-group metals.
Relative to the untreated catalyst, the ceria-coated catalyst will sustain higher catalytic activity under transient, low-temperature exhaust conditions containing H2O and NO.
Relative to the untreated catalyst, the ceria-coated catalyst will have improved durability during thermal aging and simulated mileage accumulation.
The ceria-coated catalyst will maintain low platinum-group-metal consumption.
The untreated catalyst experiences activity loss and durability degradation under transient, low-temperature exhaust conditions involving H2O, NO, and thermal aging.
The proposed effect is bounded to transient gasoline or hybrid-vehicle exhaust operation below 350°C.
The results may differ in high-temperature, ultra-lean, or static exhaust environments.
